notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity + Private control plane. Primary ask = strict throughput guarantees and predictable latency SLOs for latency-sensitive chat + reranking bundles. They operate edge devices + central orchestration; need regional reserved GPUs for failover.

Key stakeholders: Head of ML (Dr. Priya Anand), CTO (Marco Silva), Infra Lead (Jin Park). 
AE: Owen Patel; SE: Lena Morales; CSM: Hassan Qureshi.

Requirements (from discovery):
- Workloads: conversational assistant (low-latency), semantic reranking for search, embeddings batch jobs overnight.
- Latency targets: p50 ~ 40-60ms, p95 < 150ms for chat generation (up to 128 tokens). "We can't exceed 200ms at p95 for primary flows" — Head of ML.
- Throughput: sustained 350-450 QPS per region for chat routes; peak bursts to ~1k QPS (short windows). Reranking flows ~150 QPS with high fan-out. Embeddings: batch throughput ~2000 reqs/hr but not latency-critical.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to commit to reserved capacity for latency predictability, expect clear unit economics.
- Model preferences: prefer open LLMs (LlamaX-style) but will accept quantized variants; want ability to route to smaller quantized model under saturation with measurable quality regression metrics.
- Deployment constraints: VPC with private control plane; optional on-prem worker pools for EU region; customer-managed KMS; strict audit logging and retention policies.

Technical evaluation notes (POC plan):
- GPU sizing: initial ask = reserve 12 x A100-80GB equivalents in primary region + 8 x A100 in secondary region for cross-region failover. SE recommendation: two availability zones per region, start with 16 primary / 8 secondary to cover peak bursts and autoscaling buffer.
- Throughput guarantees: propose a committed throughput SLA of 400 sustained QPS with documented measurement hooks (token-level billing + tracing). Include canary ramp and synthetic load tests (see Drive PoC deck).
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 150ms for chat at 128 tokens (quantized runpaths), with fallbacks allowed if model variant triggers. Define measurement windows and exclusion policies for scheduled maintenance.
- Fallback design: multi-tier fallback policy agreed in principle: (1) local-per-client model variant (full precision) -> (2) quantized variant (4-bit) same model -> (3) smaller architecture (faster) with quality-check gating. Aim to keep generation-quality drop <3% on internal evals for critical intents. KV cache warm-up policy and prefix caching to avoid cold-start spikes.
- Cross-region failover: aim RTO < 30s for regional outage using warm standby in secondary region with async KV cache replication + traffic reroute via smart-routing policy. Discussed progressive reroute (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and synthetic probe based health checks.
- Graceful degradation: route low-priority embedding/batch jobs to alternative capacity during sustained pressure; realtime chat must keep at least degraded-mode with quantized models rather than fail to 503s.

SLA / commercial negotiation points:
- Proposed SLA tiers: 99.9% availability for dedicated endpoints; separate latency SLO with credits for p95 misses beyond agreed thresholds. Customer requested credit cap and a dedicated response SLA for major incidents (2-hour notification, 8-hour mitigation plan).
- Price levers: committed monthly GPU pool + burst capacity at fixed rate; discount thresholds at 12/24 month commits. Need engineering signoff on the exact GPU mix and support hours (24/7 on-call add-on).

POC runbook / timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-02-14: Kickoff (ff_20260214) — agreed scope and measurement KPIs.
- 2026-02-20 -> 03-05: PoC week 1 — synthetic latency + throughput runs, baseline metrics collected (see Drive logs).
- 2026-03-02: Security questionnaire submitted; awaiting SOC2 artifact and KMS integration checklist.
- 2026-03-10: SE demo of multi-tier fallback and canary rollouts; client requested deeper test of cross-region failover under cold-cache.

Open questions / blockers:
- Security: need SOC2 report and evidence of customer-managed KMS integration for encryption-in-use (HSM notes). Security team flagged data residency specifics for EU on-prem workers.
- Failover encryption: confirm end-to-end encryption between regions and whether secondary standby requires separate KMS keys.
- Quality gating: define automated quality thresholds for model-variant fallback (which metric: intent-level accuracy vs token-level perplexity?).
- Cost model: customer wants clearer burn-rate projection for burst scenarios (look at Optimize recommendations).

Linked artifacts: SLA draft (Drive), PoC perf deck (Drive), Fireflies transcripts ff_20260214_kickoff and ff_20260228_throughput_poc_call, Jira RDW-2143 (sec questions), RDW-2209 (PoC infra tuning).

Next steps (short):
- Deliver revised SLA + GPU sizing sheet by 2026-03-09 (action: Owen + Lena).
- Security sync with Redwood security on KMS + SOC2 artifacts (action: Hassan).
- Schedule cross-region cold-cache failover test with Ravencliff infra team (target week of 2026-03-15).

Recent quotes / verbatims:
- "If we lose a region we need <30s to keep latency guarantees — otherwise product is unusable" — CTO
- "We prefer fallback to a smaller model over returning errors to user; must keep quality delta small" — Head of ML

Sales play notes: emphasize dedicated's predictable throughput, Optimize module for GPU planning, and Private control plane for KMS/audit needs. Use canary + rollouts examples from other enterprise customers to reduce perceived risk.
